entities.name: PMID:27520057
observations: Prospective two-period French pediatric emergency-department study of community-acquired pneumonia prescribing in children aged 1 month–15 years.
Compared May 2009–May 2011 (3,034 evaluable children) with January–July 2012 (293 children).
Non-compliance decreased from 48.0% to 18.8%; amoxicillin monotherapy increased from 54.2% to 71.0% (p<0.001).
Authors concluded compliance significantly increased and broad-spectrum prescribing decreased, while further improvement efforts remained necessary.

entities.name: Paediatric community-acquired pneumonia
observations: Condition assessed in the prospective French network study of antibiotic prescribing compliance.

entities.name: CAP prescribing compliance improved
observations: In the French network cohort, non-compliance with antibiotic recommendations fell from 48.0% in 2009–2011 to 18.8% in 2012, with a significant adjusted period association.
Amoxicillin monotherapy increased from 54.2% to 71.0% (p<0.001), indicating a shift away from broad-spectrum or combination therapy.
